hints.title: Find the maximum as a function of p
hints.body: Hold the parameter fixed and expand as a quadratic in the input. Complete the square to find its vertex height.
hints.recap: A downward-opening quadratic reaches its maximum at the vertex.
hints.pitfall: The vertex input is different from its height.
hints.pause: Sketch the downward-opening parabola and the stated horizontal bound. Which height must be compared with it?

recall.reminder: A downward-opening quadratic reaches its maximum at the vertex.

hints.title: Apply the bound to that height
hints.body: Set your maximum-height expression strictly below the given limit. Rearrange into a quadratic inequality in p.
hints.recap: A parameter restriction comes from solving the inequality for its allowed values.
hints.pitfall: A strict bound excludes the cases where the maximum equals the limit.
hints.pause: Factor or use a squared-expression bound, then check both endpoints.

recall.reminder: A parameter restriction comes from solving the inequality for its allowed values.

solution:
For fixed p, f(x)=−x2+(p−2)x+2p. Completing the square gives f(x)=−(x−p−22)2+(p+2)24.

The square term can be zero for every real p, so the maximum value is exactly (p+2)24. The required inequality is (p+2)24<4, or −4<p+2<4.

Hence −6<p<2, option D. At either excluded endpoint the maximum is 4, and outside this interval it exceeds 4. This establishes the full parameter range.
